name: Action Construction Equipment Ltd
title: Action Construction Equipment Ltd - 532762 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 best-ever Q1 with EBITDA up 19.7% to INR170.58 cr, but gross margin fell ~140 bps on commodity costs; management pushed ~10% cumulative price and is still building a 1,000-crane tower capacity decision pending September.

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose about 19% to INR836 crore and EBITDA rose 19.66% to INR170.58 crore at a 20.40% margin, with management guiding no margin expansion.
summary.overview: Management called Q1 FY27 its best-ever first quarter on revenue and profit, with total income up about 19% YoY to INR836 crore and PAT up 22.47% to INR118.59 crore. Segment revenue for Cranes, Construction Equipment and Metal Handling rose about 22% to INR738.37 crore, while Agri Equipment booked INR42.67 crore. Commodity inflation (steel up nearly 20%, plus rubber, tyres, plastics and freight) compressed gross margin by about 140 bps YoY, which management is offsetting with price hikes totalling about 10% so far. Management declined to give a full-year revenue growth number until end-September, citing demand unpredictability and price resistance.

financial_highlights.change: up 19.66% YoY; margin up 12 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Cranes, Construction Equipment & Metal Handling revenue
financial_highlights.change: up about 22% YoY from INR605.43 crore; volumes up 17.25% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR42.67 crore revenue; INR4.34 crore margin

financial_highlights.change: contracted about 140 bps YoY per analyst; management attributed to commodity costs

segments.name: Cranes, Construction Equipment & Metal Handling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR738.37 crore (up about 22% YoY), volumes up 17.25%, margin INR134.09 crore (up 24.35%). Backhoe loaders run at about 150-160 units per quarter.

segments.name: Agri Equipment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR42.67 crore with margin INR4.34 crore (about 10% margin). Management expects agri at about 6-7% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: About 5% of Q1 revenue. Management expects 5-6% of FY27 revenue; the big defence order execution starts in August, and a repeat order above INR100 crore is expected in 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 3% of Q1 revenue, held back by shipping issues and Middle East (Saudi Arabia) shipments pending since March. Management expects 6-7% or more of FY27 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No full-year revenue growth number yet; management will give guidance by end-September 2026, after the price actions play out.
Management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q2 FY26 and similar to Q1 FY27. Historically 40-45% of revenue comes in H1 and 55-60% in H2.
Management aims to maintain operating EBITDA margin of about 15% (FY26 was a little over 15% on an operating basis) in Q2 and possibly Q3, with no planned margin expansion.
Cost inflation expected at 11-12% in total; about 10% price increases already booked; about 2% more may be needed depending on August-September commodity moves.
Capex for FY27 guided at INR200-250 crore, including about INR130-140 crore for land takeover, INR40-50 crore for Plant 9, and INR50-60 crore for upgradation, robotics and maintenance.
KATO JV to be functional by end-July 2026. Revenue contribution from Q3 FY27, with meaningful revenue from FY28.
capex_capacity: KATO JV with Japan's KATO Works: total investment about INR200 crore, of which INR100 crore cash from KATO and INR100 crore in kind from ACE (machine models, technology, infrastructure). Upgraded Indian models with KATO technology from about Q4 FY27; dedicated KATO export models in 1-2 years, with localisation targeted at 50-60%.

Plant 9 (defence-dedicated, special machines plus new products): INR40-50 crore investment, functional by end-December 2026 (Q3 FY27 to early Q4). Management expects turnover capacity of about INR500 crore. Uses the last meaningful land parcel (about 100 acres) in the existing complex.

Tower crane capacity expansion: plans ready, but start deferred. Decision in September 2026 on starting in October or deferring by 6 months. Current capacity was raised to about 1,000 cranes a year via minor rearrangements and a rented small factory about 4-5 km away.
Rough terrain forklift manufacturing started in Q1 FY27 for defence.
demand_pricing: Demand was strong till May-June 2026, and softened in the monsoon. Management says it expects growth in Hydra crane volumes (price increases and technology change had suppressed them in FY26).

Pick-and-carry mix: Hydra about 60% and new generation (NG) about 40% in FY26; management expects a return to about 60:40 in FY27, eventually settling near 50:50. Realisation expected to rise on higher tonnage models (18, 20 and 25 tonne).
Price actions: about 1-1.5% in January, 3-4% in March, and 5-6% in June (still being implemented, due to complete in July). Cumulative about 9-10%, with another 2% possible.

Commodity inflation: steel up nearly 20%, plus tyres, belts, rubber and plastics. Management estimates Q1 raw-material inflation at about 5-6% (7-8% flowed through per Sorab Agarwal), with more to hit Q2.
Competition: intensity unchanged according to management. Biggest challenge is inflation and customers' resistance to price hikes.

Predictability is the main issue; management cites the Iran/West Asia war, US tariffs and erratic monsoon. A deficient monsoon could cut Tier 2 and rural demand by 5-10%, with the effect showing in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much did defence and export orders contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the visibility for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Export was about 3% and defence about 5% of Q1 revenue. For FY27, management expects exports 6-7% or more and defence 5-6%, so the combined share will be about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can you update on the KATO JV?
qa_highlights.answer: Formalities are complete and the JV should be functional by end-July. Revenue from Q3 FY27, with meaningful revenue from FY28. Upgraded models are expected from about Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the defence order target of about INR200 crore still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to exceed it by 10-15%. A repeat order of more than INR100 crore is expected in 1-2 quarters. Small orders of INR1-5 crore come in monthly.

qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation did you see in Q1, and what is expected in Q2? Will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflation is expected at 11-12% in total, with about 10% booked. Management says there is no plan for margin expansion, only cost recovery. Price increases and inflation are expected to align by July-August.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin down about 140 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to commodity cost increases. Steel is up nearly 20%, and all other inputs have risen, with pricing actions taken to protect full-year margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the new tower crane facility and the Plant 9 facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Tower crane expansion will be decided in September (start October or defer 6 months). Plant 9 is due by end-December, with turnover of about INR500 crore, and capex for the year is INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What was the anti-dumping duty status on Chinese cranes?
qa_highlights.answer: No leads so far. Management believes the DGTR recommended the duty, but the Finance Ministry did not implement it, and says it is still hopeful.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation: management expects 11-12% in total with about 2% more to come, and any further escalation in West Asia would add to costs.
Price resistance: about 10% price increases in 6 months may slow Q2 volumes, particularly in the seasonally weak monsoon period.
Export shipments to Saudi Arabia and the Middle East were delayed by shipping issues, with about 3% of Q1 revenue at risk of further slippage.
Anti-dumping duty on Chinese cranes was not notified, leaving import competition unaddressed.
Monsoon risk: a deficient monsoon could cut rural and Tier 2 demand by 5-10% in H2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on margin recovery, but cautious on forward growth: management declined a full-year growth number until end-September, citing inflation, price resistance and geopolitical uncertainty. Answers on defence, the KATO JV and capex were specific, while demand and anti-dumping questions drew more hedged replies.
key_quotes: Against this backdrop, our company registered its best -ever Q1 performance with continued focus on disciplined execution, operational excellence and maintaining a healthy balance between growth and profitability.
So we see, obviously, there is a lot of resistance. And this is coupled at a time when the market is at its leanest because of rains.
Yes. Total investment envisaged is about INR200 crores. And INR100 crores is being put in cash by KATO.

Plant 9 defence-dedicated special machines and new products, turnover capacity about INR500 crore
Tower crane capacity expansion (plans ready, start deferred to Sept 2026 decision; current capacity about 1,000 cranes/yr)

growth.why: No full-year revenue number until end-September; Q1 total income up about 19% and Q2 guided better than Q2 FY26, backed by ~10% booked price hikes, KATO JV (Q3 FY27 revenue start) and Plant 9 (Q3 FY27), while tower crane expansion is deferred and EBITDA margin is held at ~15%.
